related_questions.question: Can transient global amnesia be caused by a stroke?
related_questions.snippet: Transient global amnesia is an episode of confusion that comes on suddenly in a person who is otherwise alert. This confused state isn't caused by a more common neurological condition, such as epilepsy or stroke.

related_questions.question: Is TGA a mini stroke?
related_questions.snippet: Is TGA a mini stroke? Transient global amnesia (TGA) isn't a mini stroke (transient ischemic attack). Even though the conditions share a word in their name and both have symptoms that come on suddenly, they're different conditions. Sudden memory loss is the main — and generally only — sign of TGA.

related_questions.question: How long does it take to recover from TGA?
related_questions.snippet: TGA is self-limited and resolves within 24 hours. There is no established treatment for episodes. The lifetime recurrence rate is 2.9% to 23.8%.

related_questions.question: What to do after transient global amnesia?
related_questions.snippet: No treatment is needed for transient global amnesia. It gets better without treatment and has no known lasting effects.

text_blocks.snippet: Transient global amnesia (TGA) and stroke, while both can cause memory loss, are distinct conditions. TGA is characterized by a sudden inability to form new memories, but it is temporary and usually resolves within 24 hours, according to MedlinePlus. Strokes, on the other hand, can cause various memory impairments, including anterograde amnesia (difficulty forming new memories), retrograde amnesia (loss of past memories), or both. TGA is not considered a type of stroke, although both can present with amnesia.
snippet_highlighted_words: TGA is characterized by a sudden inability to form new memories, but it is temporary and usually resolves within 24 hours

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: TGA is a temporary condition, resolving within 24 hours. Strokes can cause permanent or long-lasting memory deficits.

list.title: Cause:
list.snippet: TGA's exact cause is unknown, but it's not considered an ischemic event (stroke). Strokes are caused by disruptions in blood flow to the brain, either by blockage (ischemic stroke) or rupture (hemorrhagic stroke).

list.title: Memory Impairment:
list.snippet: TGA primarily affects the ability to form new memories, while strokes can affect both the formation of new memories and the recall of past memories.

list.title: Other Symptoms:
list.snippet: TGA is typically characterized by repetitive questioning and disorientation to time. Strokes can cause a wide range of symptoms depending on the affected brain area, including weakness, numbness, speech problems, and vision changes.

list.title: Risk Factors:
list.snippet: TGA is more common in older individuals and those with a history of migraines. Strokes are associated with various risk factors, including high blood pressure, high cholesterol, smoking, and heart disease.

list.title: Differential Diagnosis:
list.snippet: Doctors must differentiate between TGA and stroke, especially when amnesia is the primary symptom.

list.title: MRI:
list.snippet: MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) can help distinguish TGA from ischemic stroke by revealing characteristic lesions in the hippocampus in TGA cases.

list.title: Treatment:
list.snippet: There is no specific treatment for TGA, and episodes usually resolve on their own. Strokes require prompt medical attention and treatment to minimize brain damage.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, while both TGA and stroke can cause amnesia, they are distinct conditions with different causes, symptoms, and treatment approaches.
